questions.stem: A company applying for a Massachusetts pharmacy licence has a minority investor whose previous out-of-state pharmacy entered a consent agreement resolving a complaint, and whose separate professional licence was once suspended. The applicant company itself has a clean record. Which statements about the Board's suitability review are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The factors reach an interest holder as well as the applicant itself.
A consent agreement resolving a complaint is among the listed factors.
Only conduct at a Massachusetts pharmacy may be weighed by the Board.
Prior discipline on a separate professional licence is a listed factor.
The Board may conclude that licensing would not serve public health and safety.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is being sold. Twenty days before the closing date the buyer submits a complete licence application with the controlled substance inventory report and the bill of sale. The seller files nothing, on the basis that the buyer's application tells the Board everything it needs. Is the seller's position sound?

choices.text: No, because the outgoing licensee owes the Board its own notice of the transfer.
No, because the seller must instead surrender the licence to the Board first.
Yes, because the buyer's application was filed more than 14 days ahead.
Yes, because the inventory report identifies both pharmacies to the Board.
Yes, provided the seller countersigns the buyer's licence application.

questions.stem: A closing Massachusetts pharmacy will move its Schedule II through VI stock to a sister pharmacy. The Manager of Record has given the Board written certified-mail notice with all required particulars and the transfer is set for day 15. Which statements about what follows are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The transferor may keep a small residual stock to finish outstanding prescriptions.
An attestation confirming the inventory is filed with the Board within 30 days.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
Only the transferee's Manager of Record needs to sign the inventory report.
The transferor may possess no controlled substances after the transfer date.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts sterile compounding applicant has held a provisional licence for eleven months. It has made real progress but will not reach full compliance for another two months, and asks the Board to extend the provisional licence for that period. What is the position?

choices.text: The Board may extend it once, for a period not exceeding six months.
The Board may extend it where the applicant shows continued substantial compliance.
The Board must extend it, since full compliance is the stated objective.
The Board may convert it now and inspect for full compliance afterwards.
The provisional licence may not be renewed or extended and lapses at one year.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts wholesale drug distributor changes its designated responsible person and its warehouse address. Its compliance officer plans to report both at the next annual renewal, and adds that a director's old felony conviction for an offence unrelated to drugs cannot matter to the Board. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Both points are sound; renewal is the natural time to update the record.
The reporting plan is sound, but the conviction is a listed Board factor.
The changes go to the Board within 30 days, and any felony conviction is listed.
The changes go to the Board within 30 days, but the conviction falls outside the list.
Neither point matters, because the factors govern issuance rather than renewal.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts company holds a wholesale druggist controlled substance registration and is opening a second distribution warehouse in another city. Its counsel says the existing registration covers the new site and runs on the same two-year cycle as the group's pharmacy registrations. What is the position?

choices.text: Counsel is right on both points, since one registrant holds one registration.
Counsel is right on coverage but wrong on the cycle, which is three years.
Counsel is wrong on coverage but right that a two-year cycle applies.
Counsel is wrong on both: a separate registration is needed and the term is one year.
Counsel is wrong on coverage, and the wholesale registration has no fixed expiry.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts nuclear pharmacy is describing its services to a hospital client. Which activities fall inside the regulatory definition of radiopharmaceutical service? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Counting, dispensing, labeling and delivery of radiopharmaceuticals.
Operating the imaging equipment on which the product is later used.
Interpreting the images produced after the product is administered.
Prescribing the radiopharmaceutical for the individual hospital patient.
Advising on therapeutic values, hazards and use of radiopharmaceuticals.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts entity holds a provisional outsourcing facility registration because it had not been inspected by the FDA in the two years before its application. It has compounded a batch of sterile preparations and wants to ship them to a hospital in the Commonwealth while it waits for the inspection. May it?

choices.text: Yes, because the provisional registration authorises it to operate as a facility.
Yes, because the shipment stays inside the Commonwealth.
Yes, provided the receiving hospital records the provisional status.
No, because a provisional holder is barred from compounding until inspected.
No, because a provisional holder is permitted to compound but not to supply.

questions.stem: On a Monday a Massachusetts pharmacy discovers that a controlled substance package delivered the previous Wednesday shows signs of having been opened and resealed. Nothing is confirmed missing. The Manager of Record plans to investigate for a few days and then decide whether to report. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: A report to the Drug Control Program within 24 hours of Monday's discovery.
A report to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy within 24 hours of Monday.
A report to the Drug Control Program within 24 hours of the Wednesday delivery.
No report, because no controlled substance has been confirmed missing.
A report once the internal investigation establishes that a loss occurred.
